class.name: NetwLivenessCore
class.brief_description: Record store behind [LivenessShell]: it mints entity handles, bridges them to wire routes, holds the existence state machine, and keeps the callers waiting on a route that is not live yet.
class.description:
A record holds no [Object], which is what lets it outlive the entity it names. [constant STATE_DEAD] is a tombstone kept for the whole session so a stale packet resolves to "known but dead" instead of being mistaken for one that arrived early, and that outliving is the reason the store is here rather than in [LivenessShell]. Death is therefore a state transition and never a free. [method clear] at session teardown is the only place a record is released. [LivenessShell] owns the one instance a session has and is the surface to use. Reach for this class directly only when writing liveness itself. [codeblock] var core := NetwLivenessCore.new()
var entity := core.entity_create() var route := core.reserve_route() core.bind_route(entity, route) # core.route_state(route) == NetwLivenessCore.STATE_LIVE
core.set_state(entity, NetwLivenessCore.STATE_DEAD) # core.route_state(route) stays STATE_DEAD for the rest of the session [/codeblock] [method set_state] moves forward only and returns [code]false[/code] on a backward edge, so a caller decides for itself whether a refused edge is a bug or a stale packet to drop. [method bind_route] is the one backward door, and only from [constant STATE_DEAD] to [constant STATE_LIVE], which is the re-admission a spawn frame performs when it arrives after the despawn that tombstoned its route. A re-admission binds a fresh handle, so the superseded record keeps its tombstone and never resurrects. A reliable event that must not be lost across the spawn window parks on its route through [method when_live] instead of retrying, and one of three things happens to it. A binding that means something to waiters answers them through [method flush_live]. A deadline passing during [method poll] expires them. A route dying drops them through [method abandon_live], because a tombstoned route can never go live and a waiter on one is waiting forever. [codeblock] when_live(route, cb, deadline) ──flush_live(route)───▶ cb runs ──poll past deadline──▶ on_timeout runs ──abandon_live(route)─▶ neither runs [/codeblock] A deadline is a plain integer rather than a duration, because the counter it is measured against lives above this class: a tick clock is a session service and the record plane holds no session. So [method when_live] is told which counter its deadline belongs to, and [method poll] is handed that counter's reading again. With no clock configured the counter is this store's own frame count, which [method frame] answers and [method poll] advances. Binding never answers waiters implicitly. [method bind_routes_data] flushes because a row arriving is exactly what a waiter asked to hear about, and [method bind_route] does not, because the caller above it decides whether that particular binding is news.

method.name: abandon_live
method.description: Drops every caller waiting on [param route] without running any of them, neither the callback nor its timeout. This is what a route reaching [constant STATE_DEAD] does to its waiters: the route can never go live, so a wait on it would otherwise never end.

method.name: bind_route
method.description: Binds [param entity] to [param route] and moves it to [constant STATE_LIVE], returning [code]false[/code] when [param route] is not positive or [param entity] names no record. Re-pointing a route supersedes whatever record held it before. The superseded record keeps its own state, so a tombstone that loses its route stays dead. Waiters parked through [method when_live] are not answered here. Call [method flush_live] when this binding is the news they were waiting for.

method.name: bind_routes_data
method.description: Binds every route in [param routes] as a live record with no entity behind it, the identity a replicated row is, and answers whatever was waiting on each through [method flush_live]. A route already standing is reused rather than minted past, so a row arriving for a route an entity already holds lands on that same record. Both orderings therefore converge on one identity. A route at or below zero is skipped.

method.name: clear
method.description: Frees every record, empties the waiting room, and restarts both route numbering and the frame count. The only place a record is released.

method.name: entity_create
method.description: Mints a record and returns its handle. A fresh record carries no route and reads [constant STATE_UNKNOWN] until [method bind_route].

method.name: entity_is_valid
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while [param entity] names a record this store owns. Stays [code]true[/code] for a record in [constant STATE_DEAD], because a tombstone is a state and not a release.

method.name: flush_live
method.description: Runs every callback waiting on [param route], in the order they were parked, and releases them. The queue is emptied before the first callback runs, so a callback that parks a fresh wait on this same route is left waiting rather than answered by the flush that woke it.

method.name: frame
method.description: Returns how many times [method poll] has run this session. This is the counter a wait armed with [code]on_clock[/code] false ages against, so it is also what a caller adds a timeout to when composing a deadline.

method.name: live_routes
method.description: Returns every route currently in [constant STATE_LIVE], sorted, so two calls in one frame agree.

method.name: pending_live_count
method.description: Returns how many callers are still waiting for a binding, across every route. This is the liveness backlog: a number that climbs and never falls means events are being parked faster than routes are going live.

method.name: poll
method.description: Advances [method frame], expires every wait whose deadline has passed, and returns the routes whose last waiter expired, sorted. Pass the tick a configured clock is reading, or [code]0[/code] when there is no clock. Waits armed with [code]on_clock[/code] false ignore [param clock_tick] and age against [method frame] instead. A timeout callback runs after the waiting room is consistent again, so one that parks a fresh wait is not swept by the same pass that woke it. The returned routes are what a caller reports on: this store knows a deadline passed, and the surface above it knows how to say so.

method.name: reserve_route
method.description: Returns the next route. Routes are session-monotonic and never reused, so a route names one wire identity for the whole session even after it is tombstoned.

method.name: rid_from_route
method.description: Returns the handle bound to [param route], or an invalid [RID] when nothing is bound. Resolves a tombstoned route to the record that carries its [constant STATE_DEAD].

method.name: route_count
method.description: Returns how many routes have been bound this session, tombstones included.

method.name: route_of
method.description: Returns the route bound to [param entity], or [code]0[/code] when it is unbound or names no record.

method.name: route_state
method.description: Returns the state of [param route]. A route that was never bound reads [constant STATE_UNKNOWN], which is what distinguishes a packet that may simply be early from one naming a tombstone.

method.name: set_state
method.description: Moves [param entity] to [param state], returning [code]false[/code] when the edge would move backward or stay put, or when [param entity] names no record. See [method bind_route] for the one backward door.

method.name: state_of
method.description: Returns the state of [param entity], or [constant STATE_UNKNOWN] when it names no record.

method.name: tombstone_routes_data
method.description: Moves every route in [param routes] to [constant STATE_DEAD], the death edge of [method bind_routes_data]. A route nothing is bound to is skipped, so tombstoning a route this peer never learned about is silent rather than an error. Authority is decided above this store. The server runs it when it releases an identity and every other peer runs it when the lifecycle frame lands, so both ends reach the same state through the same code.

method.name: when_live
method.description: Parks [param callback] until [param route] reaches [constant STATE_LIVE], or runs it immediately when the route is already live. [param deadline] is an absolute reading of a counter rather than a duration, and [param on_clock] names which counter: [code]true[/code] for the tick a caller passes to [method poll], [code]false[/code] for this store's own [method frame]. [param on_timeout] runs instead of [param callback] when the deadline passes, so a caller holding state keyed on the pending route can release it rather than leak it. Several callers may wait on one route. They are answered in the order they were parked, and one expiring does not disturb the others.

constants.constant: No record is bound to the route on this peer. A packet naming it may simply be early.
The route is bound and its entity is present.
A despawn was issued with linger. The route still resolves while the entity winds down, which is what lets a late query still name a dying entity.
The route is tombstoned for the rest of the session. Only [method bind_route] leaves this state, and only as a re-admission onto a fresh handle.
